explanations: terra: God is Master of the Day of Recompense, the most compact statement of who owns the final account.

terra: The source dictionary says تَوَلَّى can mean taking office as well as turning away; in “وَإِذَا تَوَلَّىٰ” the man turns away or gains power and then corrupts the land, making that double hearing consequential.

luna: The section rejects coercion in the Prophet’s role. This verse states there is no compulsion in religion and distinguishes right guidance from error. | terra: “No compulsion in religion” states the general boundary corresponding to the Prophet's lack of coercive mastery, while grounding response in the distinction between guidance and error.

luna: The section limits the Prophet’s responsibility for people’s response to reminder. This verse says their guidance is not upon him; God guides whom He wills. | terra: “لَّيْسَ عَلَيْكَ هُدَىٰهُمْ” removes responsibility for making people guided from the Prophet and assigns guidance to God.
luna: The section says people return to God for account. This verse warns of a day when they will be returned to God and every soul paid in full for what it earned, without being wronged.

luna: The section says the Prophet’s work is reminder rather than control. This verse says if they turn away, only delivery is upon him, while God sees His servants. | terra: “If they turn away” is answered by “فَإِنَّمَا عَلَيْكَ ٱلْبَلَاغُ,” joining the source's turning-away verb to the Messenger's strictly bounded duty.

luna: The section denies the Prophet control over people and assigns punishment to God. This verse tells him he has no say in the affair, whether God turns to people in mercy or punishes them. | terra: “لَيْسَ لَكَ مِنَ ٱلْأَمْرِ شَىْءٌ” excludes the Prophet from deciding whether God accepts or punishes wrongdoers, matching the section's ownership of punishment.
terra: At judgment the Prophet is brought as a witness over his community, a defined evidentiary role distinct from controlling them or owning their account.

luna: The section notes that تَوَلَّى can have the secondary sense of taking up a task or office. This verse names أُولِي الْأَمْر, those entrusted with authority, and directs disputes back to God and the Messenger, making delegated authority distinct from the Prophet’s role as everyone’s overseer.
terra: The Prophet is told to turn aside from the hypocrites yet admonish them with penetrating speech, showing that disengagement from control can coexist with continued verbal reminder.

luna: The section says the Prophet is not a monitor over people. This verse says whoever turns away has his own path, for the Prophet was not sent as their حَفِيظ. | terra: “وَمَن تَوَلَّىٰ” is followed by God's statement that the Prophet was not sent as a guardian over them, combining the same refusal with the same denied office.
terra: When opponents secretly plot at night, “وَٱللَّهُ يَكْتُبُ مَا يُبَيِّتُونَ”; the Prophet turns aside and relies on God, joining divine recording to prophetic noncontrol.
terra: Whoever opposes the Messenger is left to what he has taken up—“نُوَلِّهِۦ مَا تَوَلَّىٰ”—and then brought to hell, giving the source's undertakes-for-himself nuance a punitive outcome.

luna: The section draws a limit around the Prophet’s task. This verse tells those addressed that if they turn away, the Messenger’s only duty is clear delivery. | terra: After “فَإِن تَوَلَّيْتُمْ,” the hearers are told that only clear conveyance rests on God's Messenger, the section's role division in one conditional sentence.

luna: The section makes the Prophet a reminder, not an overseer. This verse says only delivery is upon the Messenger and that God knows what people reveal and conceal. | terra: “The Messenger has only conveyance,” while God knows what people disclose and conceal, dividing public proclamation from comprehensive oversight.
terra: Jesus says he was a witness while among his people, but after God took him, “كُنتَ أَنتَ ٱلرَّقِيبَ عَلَيْهِمْ”; witness and ultimate watcher are sharply distinguished.
terra: The Prophet disclaims possession of God's treasuries and knowledge of the unseen and says he only follows revelation, complementing 52:37's treasury-and-control challenge.

luna: The section says the Prophet is not the one appointed to account for people. This verse tells him not to dismiss those who call on their Lord, saying their account is not upon him and his account is not upon them; it makes the boundary of حساب explicit. | terra: The Prophet has none of the believers' account upon him and they have none of his; he may not act as judge by driving them away.

luna: The section says the Prophet is not the keeper placed over people. This verse says God is dominant over His servants and sends keepers over them until death; 6:62 continues with their return and accounting before God. | terra: God is the irresistible master over His servants and sends guardians until death, locating authority and watching under His command.

luna: The section says “to Us is their return” and “their account is upon Us.” This verse likewise says they are returned to God, their true Mawla, who owns judgment and is the swiftest of accountants; 6:61 describes the keepers until death. | terra: After death people are returned to Allah, their true Master; judgment is His and He is swiftest in reckoning, closely combining 88:25–26.

luna: The section denies that the Prophet is an overseer over those who refuse the reminder. After his people reject the truth, this verse has him say that he is not their وكيل. | terra: When the Prophet's people deny the truth, he must say “لَّسْتُ عَلَيْكُم بِوَكِيلٍ,” a close first-person counterpart to “لست عليهم بمصيطر.”
terra: Those who are mindful bear none of the mockers' account; their responsibility is only a reminder, directly bringing ذِكْرَى and another person's reckoning into one boundary.
terra: The Prophet is told to remind with the Quran lest a soul be held for what it earned; reminder precedes a divine account where no patron or intercessor can replace God.
luna: The section describes the Quranic message as what brings remembrance. This verse calls the revelation a reminder for the worlds after recalling the prophets who were guided.

luna: The section says the Prophet is not a keeper over people. This verse says whoever sees benefits himself and whoever is blind bears it against himself, then states that the Prophet is not their حَفِيظ. | terra: Seeing or remaining blind benefits or harms each person, and the Prophet says he is not their guardian; response is personal rather than enforced by him.

luna: The section says the Prophet is neither their overseer nor their guardian. This verse says God did not make him حَفِيظ over them and that he is not their وكيل. | terra: God says He made the Prophet neither a guardian over the rejecters nor their agent, a direct parallel to “not a musayṭir over them.”

luna: The section says each person will return to God for account. This verse says no soul bears another’s burden, then names the return to the Lord, who will tell them what they disputed. | terra: Each soul earns only against itself, none bears another's burden, and all return to their Lord for disclosure of their disputes.
terra: The Book is sent so the Prophet may warn by it and as a reminder to believers, defining the revealed instrument and its two verbal functions.

luna: The section assigns the final accounting to God. This verse says God will question both the communities to whom messengers were sent and the messengers themselves, placing the accounting with Him.
terra: The hearers are asked to reflect that their companion is no madman but only a clear warner, defining his role amid their rejection.
terra: The Prophet disclaims power even over benefit or harm to himself and says he is only a warner and bearer of good news, ruling out the master's power implicit in musayṭir.
terra: The Prophet must command what is right and turn away from the ignorant, a stance that combines instruction with refusal to dominate the resistant.

luna: The section glosses تَوَلَّى as turning one’s back. This verse describes turning one’s back in battle and warns of returning with God’s anger, a concrete physical use of that turning-away image in a different setting.

luna: The section notes a secondary sense of و ل ي as taking up a task or office. This verse describes believing men and women as one another’s awliya and assigns them shared work: enjoining right, forbidding wrong, prayer, and almsgiving.
luna: The section says the one who turns away and disbelieves will be punished by God. This verse says that if they turn away, God will punish them with painful punishment.

terra: God, His Messenger, and believers will see people's outward work, but people then return to the Knower of seen and unseen who tells them what they did; prophetic seeing stops short of comprehensive account.
terra: Whether God shows the Prophet some promised punishment or takes him first, the people return to “Us” and God witnesses what they do, closely repeating 13:40's frame.

luna: The section transfers oversight from the Prophet to God. This verse says no matter, Quran recitation, or human act is hidden from God, down to the smallest and largest thing, all in a clear record. | terra: God is witness while any deed is done, and nothing escapes Him or the clear record; the comprehensive oversight belongs to Him.

luna: The section restricts the Prophet’s role to reminder, not control. This verse asks whether he would compel people until they became believers, making coercion the very boundary the section draws. | terra: “أَفَأَنتَ تُكْرِهُ ٱلنَّاسَ” asks whether the Prophet would compel people into faith, directly exposing the coercion excluded by the reminder's office.

luna: The section distinguishes reminder from control and later account. This verse says guidance benefits the person and misguidance falls on them, then denies that the Prophet is their وكيل. | terra: Guidance benefits oneself and error falls upon oneself, while the Prophet is not an agent over the hearers, precisely separating proclamation from outcome.
terra: The Prophet must warn that if the people turn away he fears for them a great day's punishment; he announces the danger rather than administering it.

luna: The section reduces the Prophet’s task to reminding, not controlling people. This verse calls him only a warner and says God is وكيل over all things. | terra: The Prophet is only a warner while God is agent over everything, directly distributing the two roles the section distinguishes.
terra: Noah likewise says he does not possess God's treasuries or know the unseen, showing another messenger refusing the master's resources and knowledge.

luna: The section says if people turn away, the Prophet’s duty remains reminder and the outcome belongs to God. Hud says that if they turn away he has delivered what he was sent with, and that his Lord is keeper over everything. | terra: Hud says he has conveyed what he was sent with even if his people turn away, while his Lord succeeds them and guards all things.
terra: Shuayb tells his people that he is not a guardian over them, another messenger explicitly refusing the office described by musayṭir.
terra: Joseph contrasts scattered lords with Allah, the One and Overpowering, directly testing the source definition of musayṭirūn as masters against the true sovereign.
terra: Judgment belongs only to Allah, who commanded that none but He be worshipped; exclusive account and the source definition of Allah as the worshipped One are stated together.

terra: Joseph asks to be appointed over the land's storehouses as a knowing guardian, a legitimate, specifically granted stewardship that marks the boundary around the ungranted mastery in 52:37 and 88:22.
terra: Most people will not believe however intensely the Prophet desires it, exposing the limit that makes reminder rather than control his task.
terra: He asks no payment, and the message is only “ذِكْرٌ لِّلْعَٰلَمِينَ,” completing the contrast between his desire and his assigned means.

luna: The section says the Prophet’s task is reminder and “their account is upon Us.” This verse gives the same division in one sentence: the Prophet’s is only the delivery, and the account is upon God. | terra: The ayah states the section's division almost verbatim: “عَلَيْكَ ٱلْبَلَاغُ وَعَلَيْنَا ٱلْحِسَابُ”; delivery belongs to the Messenger and reckoning to God.
terra: Immediately after 13:40's role division, God is said to judge with none able to reverse His judgment and to be swift in reckoning.
terra: Allah repays every soul for what it earned and is swift in reckoning, stating both the subject and execution of the account.
terra: The Quran is a proclamation for people so they may be warned, know that God is one, and remember; conveyance, sole worship, and recollection converge without coercion.
terra: God says every thing's treasuries are with “Us” and it descends only in a known measure, positively locating the stores whose possession 52:37 denies to people.

luna: The section says God will account for people after their return. This verse states under an oath by the Lord that He will question them all; 15:93 specifies that the question is about what they used to do.
luna: The section says people are returned for account before God. This verse identifies the subject of His questioning in 15:92: what they used to do.
terra: The Prophet must proclaim what he is commanded and turn away from the associators, combining outspoken delivery with disengagement from control.
terra: “We suffice you against the mockers” supplies the divine action paired with the Prophet's proclamation in 15:94.

luna: The section denies that the Prophet’s responsibility is to control belief. In this verse, after people excuse their disbelief by appeal to God’s will, the reply asks whether messengers have any duty beyond clear delivery. | terra: The polytheists use divine will to excuse their worship, but the ayah asks whether messengers have any task beyond clear conveyance; it distinguishes God's power from their commission.
terra: Every community received a messenger with the charge to worship Allah and avoid false powers; the universal message identifies the worshipped One without giving messengers His authority.
terra: However eager the Prophet is for their guidance, guidance is not his to produce; his concern cannot turn proclamation into control.

luna: The section says people who turn away remain outside the Prophet’s control. This verse says that if they turn away, only clear delivery is upon the Messenger. | terra: “If they turn away, only clear conveyance is upon you” directly pairs refusal with the Prophet's noncoercive task.
luna: The section says everyone returns to God for account. This verse describes the Day every soul pleads for itself and is paid in full for what it did, without being wronged.

luna: The section’s distinction between a reminder and a watcher ends in divine accounting. Here each person is brought a book on the Resurrection Day, spread open; 17:14 tells them to read it and says the self is enough as its accountant. | terra: Each person's record is brought out on resurrection as an open book, turning the hidden supervision into a personally encountered document.

luna: The section assigns حساب to God after people return. This continuation tells each person to read their book and says the self is enough as حَسِيبًا; 17:13 supplies the opened record. | terra: “Read your book” makes the person sufficient as a reckoner against himself that day; God's accounting is disclosed through the written record rather than delegated to the Prophet.

luna: The section separates the Prophet’s reminder from God’s punishment and final account. This verse says guidance benefits the person, no bearer carries another’s burden, and God does not punish until sending a messenger. | terra: Guidance or error falls on each soul, no bearer carries another's burden, and God does not punish until He sends a messenger; message and account are carefully apportioned.

luna: The section says people’s deeds will be accounted for by God. This verse says hearing, sight, and the heart will each be questioned, extending accountability to what a person perceives and intends.

luna: The section says the reminder is repeated and that some turn away. This verse says Quranic examples were varied so people might remember, yet they only become more averse. | terra: God says He has repeatedly varied matters in the Quran so people might remember, yet the repetition can increase their aversion; reminder does not control reception.
terra: When the Prophet mentions his Lord alone in the Quran, the hearers turn their backs in aversion, physically staging the source sense of تَوَلَّى as turning away.

luna: The section gives punishment to God rather than to the Prophet. This verse says God may show mercy or punish, and that the Prophet was not sent as their وكيل. | terra: God alone may show mercy or punish, while the Prophet was not sent as the people's agent; it directly assigns punishment and oversight away from him.
terra: A city's destruction or severe punishment before resurrection is “فِى ٱلْكِتَٰبِ مَسْطُورًا,” joining lined inscription to punishment administered by God.
terra: The Prophet is warned that he may consume himself with grief if people do not believe this discourse, another direct correction of responsibility for response.

luna: The section says people may turn away and disbelieve, after which God punishes. This verse commands the Prophet to state that whoever wills may believe and whoever wills may disbelieve, then names the Fire prepared for wrongdoers. | terra: The truth is announced from the Lord, belief or disbelief is left to the hearer, and God has prepared the wrongdoers' fire; proclamation and punishment remain distinct.

luna: The section links the lexical sense of سطر to lining things up and names cushions as مُصَفَّفَة in the garden. Here all are presented before their Lord in rows, making ordered lines part of the Judgment scene that leads into 18:49’s complete register. | terra: People are presented before their Lord “صَفًّا” for judgment; the source's image of things put in rows meets return and account in one scene.

luna: The section says the deeds are recorded and will be accounted for. At the Judgment, sinners see a register that leaves out neither small nor great, and find what they did present; this makes the record’s completeness concrete. | terra: The placed record omits neither small nor great and people find their deeds present, closely unfolding 54:53's “small and great inscribed.”

luna: The section describes a person turning away from reminder and later being accounted for. This verse speaks of one reminded of his Lord’s signs who turns away from them and forgets what his hands sent ahead, joining refusal to neglected deeds.
terra: “We did not send the Quran down to you that you should suffer” removes an impossible burden from the Prophet before 20:3 states its actual function.

luna: The section calls the Prophet’s task reminder and cites the one who fears. This verse says the Quran was sent as a تَذْكِرَة for whoever fears, tying the reminder to that audience. | terra: The Quran is “تَذْكِرَةً لِّمَن يَخْشَىٰ,” a reminder for one who fears, closely matching both 88:21 and the audience specified in 50:45.

luna: The section’s dictionary note glosses إله as Allah because He is the one worshipped. In this verse Allah identifies Himself as the only deity and commands Moses to worship Him, connecting the name to the gloss. | terra: “I am Allah; there is no god but Me, so worship Me ... for My remembrance” joins the source definition of Allah as the worshipped one to ذِكْر.
terra: Moses and Aaron say revelation has declared that punishment falls upon “مَن كَذَّبَ وَتَوَلَّىٰ”; denial, turning away, and divine punishment form the same sequence as 88:23–24.
luna: The section calls the cushions مُصَفَّفَة and explains the underlying sense as lining things up. In Moses’s contest, the magicians are told to come صفًّا, another concrete use of the row image.
terra: The Arabic Quran repeatedly varies warnings so people may become mindful or the text may produce remembrance in them.

luna: The section names turning away and disbelief as the response that leads to God’s punishment. This verse explicitly speaks of turning away from God’s remembrance and gives a consequence in this life and the Resurrection. | terra: Whoever turns away from God's remembrance receives a constricted life and is raised blind, a concrete consequence of refusing remembrance.
terra: God explains that His signs came and were forgotten, so the refuser is forgotten that day; judgment answers the earlier rejection of remembrance.

luna: The section transfers judgment from the Prophet to God and says people return for account. This verse draws the boundary sharply: God is not questioned about what He does, while they will be questioned.
terra: Every messenger receives the same revelation that there is no god but God and that He alone is to be worshipped, connecting messenger commission to the source's definition of Allah's name.

luna: The section says every person returns for حساب. God sets just balances for Judgment, wrongs no soul at all, and brings even a mustard seed’s weight; the verse ends by calling God an adequate accountant. | terra: God sets just balances for resurrection and brings even a mustard seed to account, concretely expressing the exact reckoning that rests on Him.
terra: The Quran is a blessed reminder sent down by God, and the hearers are asked whether they will deny it; reminder and denial face one another directly.
terra: If the people turn away, the Prophet says he has informed them equally and does not know when the promise will arrive, combining conveyance with lack of control over its fulfillment.
terra: The Prophet is commanded to tell all people that he is only a clear warner to them, another direct self-description bounded by إِنَّمَا.

luna: The section says the final account is God’s. This verse says God has a book that speaks truth and that people will not be wronged, so the divine record and just reckoning stand together. | terra: A truthful book is with God and speaks the truth about people without injustice, identifying the record that serves divine account.

luna: The section ends by saying people return to God for account. This verse asks whether people thought they were created aimlessly and would not be returned; 23:116 identifies God as the true King. | terra: The question denies that humans were created pointlessly or would not be returned to “Us,” making return essential to accountable creation.

luna: The section assigns return and account to God. This continuation names God the true King, the only deity, and Lord of the noble Throne, completing the challenge to deny return in 23:115. | terra: Allah is exalted as the true King and sole deity, identifying the sovereign to whom the return in 23:115 belongs.
terra: The disbeliever reaches what seemed like water and instead finds Allah, who pays his account in full; the image makes divine reckoning the unavoidable end.

luna: The section distinguishes the Prophet’s reminder from people’s response. This verse says if they turn away, the Messenger bears only his charge and they bear theirs; if they obey, they are guided, and only clear delivery is upon him. | terra: The Messenger bears what he was charged with and the hearers bear what they were charged with; his only duty is clear conveyance, a precise allocation of responsibility.

luna: The section assigns both return and account to God. This verse says people will return to Him and He will tell them what they did, while knowing everything. | terra: All in heaven and earth belongs to Allah; when people return to Him, He tells them what they did because He knows everything.
terra: Rejecters call the revelation old written tales and claim the Prophet had them written and dictated; their false account turns the root's writing image against the reminder itself.

luna: The section denies that the Prophet is placed over people as their overseer. After describing someone who takes desire as a god, this verse asks whether the Prophet would be that person’s وكيل. | terra: After a person takes desire as his god, the Prophet is asked whether he can be an agent over him; the object of worship and the denied supervisory role meet in one challenge.
terra: The Prophet asks no reward except that whoever wills take a path to the Lord, making freely chosen response the only requested return for his mission.
terra: The servants of the Merciful do not respond to reminders by falling deaf and blind; their receptive posture reverses the turning away developed in the source.
terra: The Prophet may nearly destroy himself because people do not believe, revealing the emotional burden that the limit on his responsibility relieves.
terra: God could send a sign that made their necks remain submissive, showing that compelling submission lies in divine power rather than the Prophet's reminder.
terra: Noah asks what knowledge he has of what his followers used to do, disclaiming the inspection of their deeds just before assigning their account to his Lord in 26:113.
terra: Noah says “إِنْ حِسَابُهُمْ إِلَّا عَلَىٰ رَبِّى,” an exact prophetic declaration that other people's reckoning rests only with the Lord.
terra: Noah concludes “إِنْ أَنَا۠ إِلَّا نَذِيرٌ مُّبِينٌ,” pairing his limited warning role with the divine account stated in 26:113.

luna: The section makes reminding the Prophet’s task and says people bear their own response. This verse commands him to recite the Quran and says whoever is guided benefits himself, while the Prophet is only among the warners.

luna: The section denies that the Prophet can control people’s response. This verse says he does not guide whom he loves; God guides whom He wills. | terra: The Prophet cannot guide even one he loves; God guides whom He wills, defining the practical limit of reminder.

luna: The section says refusal does not turn the Prophet into an overseer. Here, after the address turns to those who deny, it says the Messenger’s only duty is clear delivery. | terra: Denial does not enlarge a messenger's authority: the ayah says that only clear conveyance rests on the Messenger.
terra: Signs are with Allah and the Prophet is only a clear warner, separating divine possession of proof from his verbal commission.
terra: The Prophet must not grieve over disbelief; the disbelievers return to “Us,” who will tell them their deeds and know what hearts contain.

luna: The section says the one who turns away and disbelieves is punished by God. This verse asks who is more unjust than the person reminded of his Lord’s signs who then turns away, and says God will take retribution on the criminals. | terra: A person is reminded by the Lord's signs and then turns away; God, not the reminder, exacts vengeance from the guilty.
terra: Those who convey God's messages fear none but Him, and “كَفَىٰ بِٱللَّهِ حَسِيبًا” identifies God as the sufficient reckoner.
terra: God sends the Prophet as witness, bearer of good news, and warner; these positive commissions clarify that denying musayṭir authority does not erase every public role.
terra: The Prophet offers one admonition and is described as only a warner before severe punishment, joining a concentrated reminder to a punishment he does not execute.

luna: The section says the Prophet is not the people’s guardian and should remind those who respond. This verse says no bearer carries another’s burden, the Prophet is not their وكيل, and he warns those who fear their Lord. | terra: No burdened soul bears another's burden, and the Prophet effectively warns those who fear unseen; purification benefits the person who undertakes it.

luna: The section calls the Prophet مُذَكِّر, a reminder. This verse states that he is only a نَذِير, a warner, specifying a related but distinct part of his limited commission. | terra: “You are only a warner” is a direct restrictive formulation of the same prophetic task boundary.
terra: For some hearers, warning or not warning is equal because they will not believe, setting the limit that makes 36:11 specify the receptive audience.
terra: The Prophet can warn the one who follows the Reminder and fears the Merciful unseen; the wording limits the effective audience without making him control it.

luna: The section says the hand that writes deeds is not the Prophet’s. God says “We write” what people send ahead and their traces, and has counted everything in a clear register, specifying the divine record and its reach. | terra: God says “وَنَكْتُبُ مَا قَدَّمُوا۟ وَءَاثَٰرَهُمْ” and counts everything in a clear register, expressly assigning the record to “We.”
terra: The town's messengers answer rejection with “وَمَا عَلَيْنَآ إِلَّا ٱلْبَلَاغُ ٱلْمُبِينُ,” giving the same stance beyond Muhammad's own address.
luna: The section links the line sense of سطر with the garden cushions described as مُصَفَّفَة. This opening oath names those who line up in صفًّا, a distinct Quranic scene of ordered ranks.
luna: The section says God will account for those who turn away. This verse commands that they be stopped because they are to be questioned, making the Judgment’s interrogation explicit.

luna: The section names the cushions’ صفّ arrangement and connects it to the lexical sense of lining things up. Here the speaker says, “we are the ones in ranks,” repeating 37:1’s ranked scene in the same surah. | terra: The angels say “وَإِنَّا لَنَحْنُ ٱلصَّآفُّونَ,” an animate heavenly rank that carries the source's row image beyond cushions and written lines.
terra: Those same ranked angels glorify God; ordered rows here serve worship, distinguishing another hand and purpose behind arrangement.
terra: The rejecters are asked whether they hold the treasuries of their mighty, giving Lord, a close treasury challenge to 52:37 without its musayṭir word.
terra: The Prophet is only a warner, while Allah is the sole deity and overwhelming One, coupling his limited office with God's unique authority.

luna: The section says the Prophet’s function is reminder. This verse identifies the Quran as a reminder for the worlds, in the passage that refutes claims about the revelation. | terra: The revelation is nothing but a reminder to the worlds, another restrictive identification of the message's function.
terra: Disbelief or gratitude belongs to the person, no bearer carries another's burden, and the return to the Lord ends in disclosure of deeds.

luna: The section defines zikra as repeated remembrance. This verse says examples are given throughout the Quran so that people may remember. | terra: God sets out every kind of example in the Quran so that people may remember, describing the repeated means rather than a guaranteed outcome.

luna: The section says the Prophet is not responsible for keeping people and that their account belongs to God. This verse says the one guided benefits himself, the one astray bears it, and the Prophet is not their وكيل. | terra: After the Book is sent for humankind, guidance or error belongs to each soul and the Prophet is explicitly not their agent.
luna: The section says the Prophet is not the people’s وكيل and that God owns judgment. This verse says God created everything and is وكيل over everything, locating that encompassing role with God.

luna: The section says the return and accounting belong to God. This Judgment verse places the book, brings prophets and witnesses, and says judgment between people is done in truth; 39:70 says each soul is paid for its deeds. | terra: At judgment the book is set down and prophets and witnesses are brought while God judges in truth, locating each participant without confusing witness with judge.

luna: The section gives حساب to God. This Judgment verse says every soul is paid in full for what it did, while God knows what they do, showing the personal outcome of that account. | terra: Every soul is paid in full for what it did and God knows their deeds best, completing the account scene of 39:69.
terra: When Allah alone was invoked people disbelieved, but accepted partners; the ayah concludes that judgment belongs to Allah, the Most High and Great.
terra: On the day all are exposed, God asks whose kingdom it is and answers that it belongs to Allah alone, excluding every rival master.

luna: The section says the final account and punishment are God’s. This verse says the day every soul is repaid for what it earned, with no injustice. | terra: Every soul is repaid for what it earned, without injustice, and Allah is swift in account; this states the divine execution of the section's assigned reckoning.
terra: Whether the Prophet sees part of what is promised or dies first, the people are returned to “Us”; fulfillment and return remain God's affair.
terra: The message comes as good news and warning, yet most people turn away and do not hear; their refusal remains distinct from the messenger's act.
terra: If the hearers turn away, the Prophet's response is to say he has warned them of a thunderbolt, keeping his act verbal while judgment remains God's.

luna: The section denies that the Prophet is people’s keeper. This verse explicitly assigns حفيظ status over them to God and says the Prophet is not their وكيل. | terra: God is guardian over those who take patrons besides Him, while the Prophet is not their agent; the ayah assigns the supervisory office to its true holder.
luna: The section says the Prophet is not the final judge and that account belongs to God. This verse says that whatever people differ over, its judgment belongs to Allah.
terra: The Prophet declares our deeds are ours and yours are yours; God will gather everyone and to Him is the destination, separating responsibility before reunion.

luna: The section says the Prophet is not a keeper over people. This verse says he was not sent as their حَفِيظ and that only clear delivery is upon him. | terra: The ayah expressly says the Prophet was not sent as their guardian and that only conveyance is upon him, matching both halves of the section's limit.

luna: The section says the exception to reminder is one who turns away, followed by God’s judgment. This verse describes one who turns aside from the remembrance of the Merciful, to whom God assigns a companion that leads him away.
terra: If God takes the Prophet away, “We” will exact retribution from the rejecters, explicitly removing punishment from the Prophet's hand.
terra: If God instead shows him what they were promised, God remains fully powerful over them; either branch keeps enforcement divine.

luna: The section distinguishes the Prophet from a recorder who watches people’s states and writes their deeds. When deniers suppose their secret speech is unheard, the verse answers that God’s messengers with them are writing it down. | terra: God hears secret speech and His messengers beside the speakers write it down, supplying the true unseen surveillance and record.

luna: The section says the Prophet’s task is reminder, while those who reject it face their promised outcome. This verse tells the Prophet to leave the deniers in their talk and play until they meet the promised day.
terra: The Prophet is told to pardon the rejecters and say peace, while their eventual knowing remains future; his immediate posture is separated from judgment.

luna: The section says people return to God for their account. This Judgment scene shows every community kneeling and being called to its book, with each repaid for what it did; 45:29 describes the book’s truth and its writing.

luna: The section says the Prophet is not the one who keeps the record and that God will account for deeds. At the Judgment, each community’s book speaks truth, and God says it has been copying what they did. | terra: God's book speaks against people in truth because “إِنَّا كُنَّا نَسْتَنسِخُ مَا كُنتُمْ تَعْمَلُونَ,” making their works the copied record used in judgment.
terra: Those who disbelieve turn away from what they were warned of, restaging refusal after warning without making the warner its enforcer.

luna: The section says the Prophet’s task is reminder, not command over outcomes. This verse says he follows only what is revealed and is only a clear warner. | terra: The Prophet says he only follows what is revealed and is only a clear warner, sharply limiting both his initiative and his commission.
terra: The Bedouins may obey and receive good reward or turn away and be punished by God; their choice and God's requital mirror the section's division.

luna: The section describes a watcher set over people who attends their state and writes their action. Here two receivers sit on the right and left; 50:18 says each spoken word has a ready observer. | terra: The two receivers seated to right and left receive each person's deeds, staging the assigned recorders rather than prophetic supervision.

luna: The section’s lexical gloss calls a watcher a رَقِيب who attends to what is entrusted to him. This verse says each word has رَقِيبٌ عَتِيدٌ, completing 50:17’s scene of two receivers. | terra: No word is uttered without an attendant observer ready to record it, the concrete watcher-writer behind the section's dictionary image.

luna: The section describes people returning for account and rejects the Prophet as their overseer. This verse says each soul arrives with a driver and a witness; 50:22 describes the unveiling of what had been overlooked.

luna: The section says people will return for God’s account. This verse says the person had been heedless of this day, then has the covering removed; 50:21 introduces each soul with a driver and witness.

luna: The section says “remind” and denies that the Prophet is set over people as a controller. This verse says he is not a جَبَّار over them and commands him to remind by the Quran whoever fears God’s warning. | terra: “وَمَا أَنتَ عَلَيْهِم بِجَبَّارٍ” denies the Prophet coercive mastery, then “فَذَكِّرْ بِٱلْقُرْءَانِ” assigns him reminder for one who fears the warning.
terra: The Prophet is told to turn away from the rejecters and is not blameworthy, immediately before being told still to remind in 51:55.

luna: The section defines tezkire as a means of remembering and makes reminder the Prophet’s task. This verse commands reminder because the reminder benefits believers. | terra: “وَذَكِّرْ فَإِنَّ ٱلذِّكْرَىٰ تَنفَعُ ٱلْمُؤْمِنِينَ” repeats the command and identifies those who benefit rather than making the Prophet responsible for all responses.

luna: The section’s س ط ر discussion moves from rows to writing. Here the oath names a كِتَابٍ مَسْطُورٍ, a written book; it supplies the same root in the writing sense. | terra: “وَكِتَٰبٍ مَّسْطُورٍ” gives the same س ط ر sense as an inscribed book, near the surah's later challenge about who the controllers are.
terra: The open parchment supplies the surface on which the neighbouring “inscribed book” is set out in lines.

luna: The section begins with the command to remind and rejects a controlling role. This verse says “so remind” and denies that the Prophet is a soothsayer or madman, framing reminder as his actual commission. | terra: “فَذَكِّرْ” remains the Prophet's act despite accusations that he is a soothsayer or madman; rejection changes neither his task nor his authority.

luna: The section says the Prophet is no مُصَيْطِر and that rejecting people are not overseers either. This other Quranic use asks whether the deniers possess their Lord’s خزائن or are themselves مُصَيْطِرُون, locating such authority beyond them. | terra: The only other Quranic مُصَيْطِرُون asks whether the rejecters possess the Lord's treasuries or are themselves the controllers, denying them the mastery denied to the Prophet.

luna: The section says the Prophet is not the overseer who imposes the outcome. This verse tells him to leave the deniers until they meet the day promised to them, assigning the encounter to God’s coming judgment.

luna: The section’s exception turns away and disbelieves; the previous surah’s sequence likewise says one avoids the reminder. This verse says to leave the one who turns away from God’s remembrance and seeks only this nearer life; 53:30 says God knows who strays and who is guided. | terra: The Prophet is told to turn aside from one who has turned from God's remembrance and wants only the nearer life, bounding his pursuit of the refuser.

luna: The section says the turn-away is followed by God’s punishment and that return is to Him. This continuation says God knows who has strayed and who is guided, completing 53:29’s person turning away from remembrance.
terra: The Prophet is told to turn away from the rejecters while the divine caller summons them to the dreadful event, handing the scene from reminder to judgment.
terra: The humbled dead emerge from graves like scattered locusts, supplying the returned people in the judgment scene opened by 54:6.
terra: They hasten to the caller and name it a hard day, completing the consequence toward which the Prophet was told simply to step aside.

luna: The section says remembrance is repeated and that the Prophet brings the Quran to mind. After Noah’s people in the Qamar narrative, this refrain says the Quran is made easy for remembrance and asks who will remember. | terra: God has made the Quran easy for remembrance and asks whether anyone will take heed; its repeated refrain enacts the source definition of zikrā as abundant repetition.

luna: The section connects reminder with people’s response and with accounts of earlier peoples. After the account of ʿAd, the same refrain says the Quran is easy for remembrance and asks who will remember. | terra: The same invitation to remember is repeated after a second warning narrative, making recurrence itself part of the reminder.

luna: The section connects reminder with the response of those who hear it. After Thamud’s rejection, this repeated Qamar refrain asks who will remember the Quran made easy for remembrance. | terra: The refrain returns after another destroyed people, again offering remembrance without compelling it.

luna: The section describes a reminder that may be accepted or refused and ends with punishment. After the account of Lot’s people, this refrain again asks who will remember the Quran made easy for remembrance. | terra: Its fourth occurrence completes the surah's sustained repetition of the invitation to take reminder.

luna: The section connects the overseer’s supposed writing of deeds to God’s record. This preceding Qamar verse says everything they did is in the writings; 54:53 specifies that every small and great thing is inscribed. | terra: “وَكُلُّ شَىْءٍ فَعَلُوهُ فِى ٱلزُّبُرِ” identifies deeds as the contents of the records whose lined inscription is stated in 54:53.

luna: The section links 88:22’s مُصَيْطِر to the root س ط ر and says the true record is God’s. In the Qamar passage about earlier peoples, مُسْتَطَر states that every small and great thing is written, making that transfer of record-keeping explicit. | terra: “وَكُلُّ صَغِيرٍ وَكَبِيرٍ مُّسْتَطَرٌ” uses the section's س ط ر root for every small and great thing entered in lines, locating the comprehensive record with God.
terra: God has counted deeds people themselves forgot and is witness over everything, directly grounding the final account in divine preservation.

luna: The section’s صفّ image is a row of garden cushions, while this verse uses صفًّا for believers fighting in God’s path, like a solid structure. It makes the same ordered line serve a different, active purpose.

luna: The section gives the Prophet reminder rather than oversight. This verse says that if people turn away, the Messenger’s only duty is clear delivery. | terra: The ayah again makes turning away the hearers' act and clear conveyance the Messenger's sole obligation.
terra: The keepers of hell ask each arriving group whether a warner came, placing human warning before divine punishment and naming different agents at each stage.
terra: The condemned admit that a warner came and that they denied him, confirming rejection rather than failed coercion as the path to punishment.
terra: Knowledge of the promised judgment is only with Allah, while the Prophet is only a clear warner; knowledge and warning are allotted to different speakers.

luna: The section explains سطر as a line of writing and connects it to the record of deeds. This Quranic oath invokes the pen and what it writes, giving the root’s writing sense a direct Quranic occurrence. | terra: The oath by the pen and “مَا يَسْطُرُونَ” presents the source root's basic act of putting things into written lines.
terra: God tells the Prophet to leave to Him whoever denies this discourse, then promises a hidden divine process of requital.

luna: The section calls the Prophet a reminder and defines tezkire as something that brings remembrance. After the accusation that the Prophet is a madman, this verse says the Quran is a reminder for the worlds. | terra: The Quran is only a reminder to the worlds despite the rejecters' hostile accusation, preserving its function under opposition.
terra: The person given his book in his right hand invites others to read it, staging the record as publicly available evidence.
terra: He says he was certain he would meet his account, linking the readable book in 69:19 to reckoning.
terra: The person given his book in his left hand wishes he had never received it, reversing the right-hand record scene.
terra: He wishes he had never known his account, identifying the feared meaning of the book received in 69:25.

luna: The section says those who turn away will meet God’s punishment. This verse tells the Prophet to leave the deniers until they meet their promised day; 70:43 describes their emergence from graves to the caller.

luna: The section says people return for account and punishment. This verse depicts them emerging quickly from their graves toward the caller on that promised day; 70:42 names the meeting awaiting the deniers.
terra: Whoever turns away from the Lord's remembrance is led by Him into mounting punishment, directly joining refusal of remembrance to divine requital.
terra: The Prophet is commanded to say he possesses neither harm nor right direction for the hearers, a direct denial of controlling power.
terra: He cannot protect even himself from God and has no refuge apart from Him, sharpening the absence of delegated mastery stated in 72:21.
terra: His exception is conveyance of God's messages; disobedience then meets God's enduring fire, joining limited mission to divine punishment.
terra: God tells the Prophet to leave the comfortable deniers to Him and grant them a little respite, a vivid handoff of the rejecters' case.

luna: The section defines تذكرة as a thing that brings remembrance and says the Prophet’s role is reminder. This verse calls the revelation a تَذْكِرَة and lets whoever wills take a path to their Lord. | terra: The revelation is a reminder and whoever wills may take a path to the Lord, another formulation of offered recollection rather than compelled response.
terra: “Leave Me with the one I created alone” assigns dealing with the rejecting opponent directly to God.

luna: The section says a person who turns away and disbelieves faces God’s account. This verse says every soul is held by what it earned, expressing personal accountability without making the Prophet its keeper.
terra: “فَمَا لَهُمْ عَنِ ٱلتَّذْكِرَةِ مُعْرِضِينَ” stages people actively turning away from the reminder itself.

luna: The section names a reminder as the instrument that brings something back to mind. This verse says the Quran is a تَذْكِرَة; 74:55 gives the hearer’s choice to remember. | terra: “كَلَّآ إِنَّهُۥ تَذْكِرَةٌ” repeats the identification of revelation as the reminder after the scene of aversion.

luna: The section says the Prophet reminds but does not control the response. This verse says whoever wills may remember the تذكرة named in 74:54; 74:56 bounds that will by God’s will. | terra: “فَمَن شَآءَ ذَكَرَهُۥ” makes remembering the hearer's chosen response rather than an act forced by the Messenger.

luna: The section gives the Prophet a limited role and God final authority over punishment and account. This verse says people do not remember unless God wills, completing 74:54–55’s reminder and choice. | terra: Their willing does not escape God's will, and He alone is worthy of fear and forgiveness; this qualifies freedom of response without transferring control to the Prophet.
terra: “وَلَٰكِن كَذَّبَ وَتَوَلَّىٰ” repeats the paired denial and turning away of 88:23 in another judgment passage.

luna: The section’s reminder leaves the hearer responsible for a response. This verse says the revelation is a تَذْكِرَة and whoever wills may take a path to their Lord; 76:30 adds that human willing remains under God’s will. | terra: “This is a reminder; whoever wills may take a path to his Lord” repeats the hearer's willing response to revelation.

luna: The section denies the Prophet control over people and assigns final judgment to God. This verse says people do not will unless God wills, completing 76:29’s invitation to choose a path. | terra: Human willing remains within God's will, a neighbouring qualification that prevents noncoercion from being mistaken for independence from God.
terra: “We enumerated everything in a book” assigns exhaustive recording to the divine speaker and gives the section's line-by-line image a comprehensive object.

luna: The section connects the cushion word مُصَفَّفَة with the meaning of things set in rows. Here the Spirit and angels stand صفًّا on the day they rise, placing the same order in a Judgment scene. | terra: At judgment the Spirit and angels stand in a row and speak only by the Merciful's permission, joining ordered ranks to exclusive divine authority.
terra: Pharaoh denies and disobeys the warning, beginning another refusal-and-punishment sequence parallel to 88:23–24.
terra: He then turns his back and strives, making the physical act behind تَوَلَّى explicit.
terra: Pharaoh claims to be the people's highest lord, embodying the false human mastery that the section denies.
terra: Allah seizes that claimant in punishment for the latter and former offense, restoring punishment and mastery to God.

luna: The section says the Prophet reminds those who fear. This verse states directly that he is only a warner for the one who fears the Hour. | terra: “إِنَّمَآ أَنتَ مُنذِرُ مَن يَخْشَىٰهَا” uses the same restrictive stance: he is only a warner to one who fears the Hour.
terra: The Prophet “frowned and turned away,” using the section's تَوَلَّى scene inside the very passage that will identify revelation as a reminder.
terra: The blind seeker coming to the Prophet identifies the person from whom he turned in 80:1 and anchors the correction of how a reminder meets its hearer.
terra: The rebuke asks whether the approaching man might purify himself, showing that the result of the encounter remains a possibility rather than the Prophet's possession.
terra: The man may remember and have the reminder benefit him, stating the causal reach of reminder without guaranteeing response.
terra: The Prophet attends to the self-satisfied person, beginning the correction of how he distributes his finite attention as a reminder.
terra: “You attend to him” identifies the Prophet's mistaken prioritization, which the reminder scene then reverses.
terra: The Prophet is not responsible if the self-satisfied hearer does not purify himself, a direct limit on responsibility for response.
terra: The other hearer comes striving, supplying the willing approach to reminder that contrasts with turning away.
terra: That seeker fears, matching the section's recurring description of the person for whom warning and reminder work.
terra: The Prophet is distracted from the fearful seeker, the specific error corrected before revelation is named a reminder in 80:11.

luna: The section names tezkire as a means of bringing something to mind. This verse calls the Quran a تَذْكِرَة; 80:12 says whoever wishes may remember it. | terra: “كَلَّا إِنَّهَا تَذْكِرَةٌ” names the revelation itself as a reminder, the instrument by which something is brought back to mind in the source definition.

luna: The section says reminder leaves room for a person’s response. Here whoever wishes may remember the تذكرة named in 80:11. | terra: “فَمَن شَآءَ ذَكَرَهُۥ” leaves taking the reminder to the willing hearer, marking the same boundary between reminding and controlling response.
terra: The reminder of 80:11 is located in honored pages, bringing the offered recollection into a written object.
terra: Those pages are raised and purified, continuing the material setting of the reminder introduced in 80:13.
terra: The pages are “by the hands of scribes,” naming a proper writing hand immediately after the reminder passage, just as the section distinguishes its writer from the Prophet.
terra: The scribes are noble and righteous, completing the neighbouring identification of the hands that carry the written reminder.

luna: The section calls the Prophet a reminder and defines tezkire as what brings remembrance. This verse says the Quran is a ذكر for the worlds; 81:28 names its audience as those who choose uprightness. | terra: The Quran is nothing but a reminder to the worlds, identifying the message by the same function assigned to its bearer.

luna: The section allows for people to respond differently to reminder. This verse addresses those among the hearers who will to be upright; 81:29 says even their will is within God’s will. | terra: The reminder addresses whoever wills to go straight, placing response with the hearer.

luna: The section distinguishes the Prophet’s limited role from God’s authority over outcomes. This verse says people do not will unless God wills, completing 81:27–28’s reminder and response. | terra: The hearer's will depends on the will of Allah, Lord of the worlds, completing the boundary around human response.

luna: The section rejects the Prophet’s role as keeper over people. This Judgment passage instead introduces keepers assigned over them; 82:11 identifies them as writers and 82:12 says they know what people do. | terra: “وَإِنَّ عَلَيْكُمْ لَحَٰفِظِينَ” names actual guardians over people, the office explicitly denied to the Prophet.

luna: The section says the true record of deeds belongs to God. Here the keepers introduced in 82:10 are explicitly كِرَامًا كَاتِبِينَ, “honorable writers”; 82:12 specifies what their record concerns. | terra: Those guardians are “كِرَامًا كَٰتِبِينَ,” joining watching to writing exactly as the source definition of musayṭir does.

luna: The section describes deeds being written for later account. This verse says the appointed writers know what people do, completing 82:10–11’s scene of record-keepers. | terra: The guardian-scribes know what people do, completing the supervisory scene while distinguishing its agents from the Messenger.
terra: On the day no soul controls anything for another and “ٱلْأَمْرُ يَوْمَئِذٍ لِّلَّهِ,” all creaturely mastery gives way to God's exclusive command.
terra: The wicked have a record in Sijjin, beginning a judgment passage in which their deeds are fixed in writing.
terra: That record is “a book inscribed,” the concrete written form of the wicked person's account.
terra: The righteous likewise have a record in Illiyyin, showing that comprehensive recording covers the opposite outcome too.
terra: The righteous record too is “a book inscribed,” repeating the fixed written account across both groups.
terra: Those brought near witness the righteous record, distinguishing witnesses to the account from its divine owner.

luna: The section says people return to God for account. This Judgment passage begins the two outcomes with the person given his book in his right hand; 84:8 says he will have an easy account. | terra: Receiving one's book in the right hand begins the favourable form of the final account.

luna: The section assigns حساب to God. This verse says the person who receives his book in his right hand will be given an easy account, completing 84:7; 84:9 describes his return happy. | terra: That person will be reckoned with an easy reckoning, an explicit instance of the ح س ب outcome that belongs to God.
luna: The section says people return to God and are accounted for. This verse shows the positive outcome as the person returns to his people joyfully after the easy account of 84:8.

luna: The section says the one who turns away will face punishment after account. This verse presents the other Judgment outcome: the person receives his book behind his back; 84:11 gives his response. | terra: Receiving the book behind one's back supplies the contrary record scene.

luna: The section says God punishes the one who turned away. Here the person whose book is given behind his back calls for destruction, after the scene in 84:10 and before the Fire in 84:12. | terra: The recipient of that record calls for destruction, the immediate response to the unfavourable account.

luna: The section says God gives the greatest punishment after people return to Him. This verse names the outcome for the person whose book is behind his back: he enters a blazing Fire. | terra: He enters a blazing fire, completing the movement from written account to divinely administered punishment.
terra: Every soul has a guardian over it, affirming real supervision while leaving the section's denial that the Prophet is that guardian intact.

luna: The section cites the previous surah’s sequence: remind, then people respond differently. This verse commands reminder when it benefits; 87:10 identifies the one who will remember, and 87:11 the one who turns away. | terra: “فَذَكِّرْ إِن نَّفَعَتِ ٱلذِّكْرَىٰ” gives the same command to remind and begins the exact response-and-judgment sequence invoked by the section.

luna: The section cites the response to reminder: the one who fears remembers, while the denier turns away. This verse says the reminder will be taken by the one who fears; 87:9 gives the command and 87:11 the contrary response. | terra: The one who fears will receive the reminder, matching the receptive addressee in 50:45 and supplying the first response in the sequence begun at 87:9.

luna: The section says the one who turns away and disbelieves receives God’s punishment. This verse says the most wretched will avoid the reminder; 87:12 names the great Fire that follows. | terra: The most wretched avoids the reminder, paralleling the person who turns away in 88:23 and moving the neighbouring sequence from reminder to refusal.

luna: The section cites the sequence in which one avoids the reminder and God punishes. This verse names the great Fire entered by the most wretched, completing 87:11’s refusal and leading toward the section’s punishment. | terra: The refuser enters “ٱلنَّارَ ٱلْكُبْرَىٰ,” the greatest fire, a direct counterpart to the greatest punishment that God administers in 88:24.

luna: The section cites the previous surah’s sequence from reminder to avoidance and the great Fire. This verse says the one in that Fire neither dies nor lives, completing the consequence named in 87:12. | terra: The neighbour explains that the entrant into the greatest fire neither dies nor lives, extending the punishment invoked by the section beyond the shared “greatest” wording.

luna: The section cites the sequence in which the fearful remember and the most wretched avoid the reminder. This next verse names the contrasting outcome: success belongs to the one who purifies himself. | terra: The person who purifies himself succeeds, providing the positive hearer-side result after the reminder and greatest-fire sequence.

luna: The section links reminder with the response of the one who fears. This verse says the successful person remembers his Lord’s name and prays, completing 87:14’s description of success. | terra: He remembers his Lord's name and prays, continuing the receptive alternative to avoidance of the reminder.
luna: The section cites reminder, refusal, and the great Fire. This verse gives a motive for refusal: people prefer the nearer life; 87:17 contrasts the hereafter as better and more enduring.
luna: The section says the one who rejects reminder faces the great Fire. This verse contrasts that nearer-life preference with the hereafter, which is better and more enduring, completing 87:16.

luna: The section denies that the Prophet is the overseer and gives punishment to God. After recalling destroyed peoples, this verse says the Lord is لَبِالْمِرْصَادِ, placing the watchful station with God.

luna: The section links lined cushions with the sense of صفّ and places their arrangement beside God’s later accounting. Here the angels stand صفًّا صفًّا; 89:23 continues with Hell brought near. | terra: The angels come “صَفًّا صَفًّا” at the final judgment, another meeting of arrangement in rows with the account scene.

luna: The section says God punishes the one who turns away and disbelieves. In this Judgment passage, Hell is brought forward; 89:24 shows the person remembering too late and wishing he had sent something ahead.
luna: The section says a person’s deeds are accounted for after return. This verse shows the person remembering and regretting what he did when Hell is brought forward in 89:23.
luna: The section says Allah gives the greatest punishment to the one who turns away. This verse says no one punishes as He punishes.
luna: The section gives punishment to Allah rather than the Prophet. This verse says no one binds as He binds, emphasizing that final restraint belongs to God.

luna: The section places Paradise’s furnishings beside the later return to God. This verse addresses the tranquil soul before the command to return in 89:28, introducing the rewarded side of the Judgment scene.
luna: The section says “to Us is their return.” This verse commands the pleased and accepted soul to return to its Lord, followed by entry among God’s servants in 89:29 and into His Garden in 89:30.

luna: The section joins return to God with the Garden scene whose cushions are arranged. This verse invites the returned soul to enter among God’s servants; 89:30 completes the invitation with entry into His Garden.
luna: The section begins with ordered furnishings in the Garden and ends with people returning for account. This verse completes the positive Judgment outcome by inviting the soul into God’s Garden.

luna: The section connects turning away and disbelief with God’s punishment. This verse warns of a blazing Fire; 92:15 says only the most wretched will enter it, and 92:16 identifies him as the denier who turns away.

luna: The section links a person’s turning away to the punishment God gives. This verse says only the most wretched enters the blazing Fire named in 92:14; 92:16 specifies his denial and turning away. | terra: Only the most wretched enters the blazing fire, beginning a close parallel to the 87 and 88 sequences.

luna: The section’s exception is the one who turns away and disbelieves, followed by God’s punishment. This verse describes the same figure as one who كَذَّبَ وَتَوَلَّى, after the warning of the Fire in 92:14–15. | terra: “ٱلَّذِى كَذَّبَ وَتَوَلَّىٰ” identifies that fire's person by the same denial and turning away as 88:23.
terra: “To your Lord is the return” supplies the destination behind God's sight in 96:14 and the denier's turning in 96:13.
terra: The ayah isolates the case “إِن كَذَّبَ وَتَوَلَّىٰ,” the same paired human response that precedes punishment in the source image.
